**Sébastien Eugène Emile Ogier** (French pronunciation: [[sebastjɛ̃ ɔʒje]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")[rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rallying "Rallying") driver, competing for the [Toyota Gazoo Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_Gazoo_Racing "Toyota Gazoo Racing") Team in the [World Rally Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Rally_Championship "World Rally Championship") (WRC). He was teamed with [co-driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Co-driver "Co-driver") [Vincent Landais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Landais "Vincent Landais").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-:0-2) He has won nine [World Rally Drivers' Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Rally_Championship_Drivers'_champions "List of World Rally Championship Drivers' champions") including six consecutive titles from [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Rally_Championship "2013 World Rally Championship") to [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_World_Rally_Championship "2018 World Rally Championship"), in addition to [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_World_Rally_Championship "2020 World Rally Championship"), [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_World_Rally_Championship "2021 World Rally Championship") and [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Rally_Championship "2025 World Rally Championship"), and is the joint most successful WRC driver together with [Sébastien Loeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Loeb "Sébastien Loeb") (nine titles each). He has achieved 69 rally victories and is one of the only two drivers (with [Juha Kankkunen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juha_Kankkunen "Juha Kankkunen")) to have won the World Championship with three different manufacturers. He holds various WRC records including the most drivers' championship points overall, biggest points gap with the championship runner-up, most stage victories and points in a single season.
Ogier started his rally career in France in 2005 and won the [Peugeot 206](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peugeot_206 "Peugeot 206") Cup in 2006. He won the title in his first season in the [Junior World Rally Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_World_Rally_Championship "Junior World Rally Championship"), driving a [Citroën C2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn_C2 "Citroën C2") in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_World_Rally_Championship "2008 World Rally Championship"). He debuted in the World Rally Championship at the [2008 Rally Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Rally_Mexico "2008 Rally Mexico") and scored a point in his first race after finishing eighth. He drove a [World Rally Car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Rally_Car "World Rally Car") for the first time, a [Citroën C4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn_C4 "Citroën C4") in [2008 Rally GB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Rally_GB "2008 Rally GB") and was promoted to a full-time drive for the [next season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Rally_Championship "2009 World Rally Championship") with the [Citroën Junior Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn_Junior_Team "Citroën Junior Team"). He got his first podium in the [2009 Acropolis Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Acropolis_Rally "2009 Acropolis Rally") after securing a second-place finish. He drove select races for the [Citroën World Rally Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn_World_Rally_Team "Citroën World Rally Team") in the [2010 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_World_Rally_Championship "2010 World Rally Championship") and took his maiden WRC win in the [2010 Rally de Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Rally_de_Portugal "2010 Rally de Portugal").
Ogier secured a full time drive with the Citroën factory team for the [2011 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_World_Rally_Championship "2011 World Rally Championship"). Ahead of the [2012 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_World_Rally_Championship "2012 World Rally Championship"), he joined the [Volkswagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen "Volkswagen") team and drove a [Škoda Fabia S2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%A0koda_Fabia_S2000 "Škoda Fabia S2000"). He drove The [Volkswagen Polo R WRC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen_Polo_R_WRC "Volkswagen Polo R WRC") for the first time in the [2013 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Rally_Championship "2013 World Rally Championship"), in which, he won his first WRC Drivers title with nine rally victories from 13 events. He won a further three consecutive titles in [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Rally_Championship "2014 World Rally Championship"), [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Rally_Championship "2015 World Rally Championship"), and [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_World_Rally_Championship "2016 World Rally Championship"). He won a further two titles in the next two seasons, driving the [Ford Fiesta WRC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Fiesta_WRC "Ford Fiesta WRC") before finishing third in the [lone season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_World_Rally_Championship "2019 World Rally Championship") back with the Citroën team. He moved to [Toyota Gazoo Racing WRT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_Gazoo_Racing_WRT "Toyota Gazoo Racing WRT") before the [2020 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_World_Rally_Championship "2020 World Rally Championship") and won the two titles in 2020, and [2021 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_World_Rally_Championship "2021 World Rally Championship") while driving a [Toyota Yaris WRC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_Yaris_WRC "Toyota Yaris WRC"). Since the [2022 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Rally_Championship "2022 World Rally Championship"), he has been competing in select rallies with the Toyota team.
Ogier has also competed in the [Intercontinental Rally Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_Rally_Challenge "Intercontinental Rally Challenge"), and [Porsche Supercup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porsche_Supercup "Porsche Supercup"). Apart from rallying, he tested a [Red Bull Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Racing "Red Bull Racing") [RB7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RB7 "RB7") [Formula one](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_one "Formula one") car in 2017. He also took part in the [Race of Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_of_Champions "Race of Champions") in 2011, and drove a [Ferrari F430 Scuderia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_F430_Scuderia "Ferrari F430 Scuderia") in the 2011 [French GT Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_GT_Championship "French GT Championship"). He participated in three races in the [2022 FIA World Endurance Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIA_World_Endurance_Championship "2022 FIA World Endurance Championship") including the [24 Hours of Le Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24_Hours_of_Le_Mans "24 Hours of Le Mans") with the [Richard Mille Racing Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Mille_Racing_Team "Richard Mille Racing Team").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-:0-2)
## Rally career

### Early years (2005–2007)
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years \(2005–2007\)")]
Ogier's rally career began in 2005 when he won the French Federation's Rallye Jeunes[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-3) and was rewarded with a place in the Peugeot 206 Cup for the following season. Teamed with [co-driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Co-driver "Co-driver") [Julien Ingrassia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Ingrassia "Julien Ingrassia"), he claimed a podium at Terre des Cardabelles and sixth place in the championship along with the Best Rookie award.
In 2007, Ogier won the [Peugeot 206](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peugeot_206 "Peugeot 206") Cup with four victories (Diois, Langres, Causses, Touquet) and two second places (Alsace-Vosges, Limousin). He also won the Rallye Hivernal des Hautes-Alpes. In April 2007, he took part in his first regional rally (Rallye du Quercy) placing third overall in a Peugeot 206 XS.
Ogier received the _Espoir Echappement de l’année_ award, an honorific prize from professionals and fans, joining past winners [Didier Auriol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Didier_Auriol "Didier Auriol"), [François Delecour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Delecour "François Delecour") and [Sébastien Loeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Loeb "Sébastien Loeb").

#### JWRC Champion

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier_-_2008_Rallye_de_France_SS12.jpg/250px-S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier_-_2008_Rallye_de_France_SS12.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier_-_2008_Rallye_de_France_SS12.jpg)Ogier at the [2008 Tour de Corse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Tour_de_Corse "2008 Tour de Corse")
In the [2008 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_World_Rally_Championship_season "2008 World Rally Championship season"), Ogier moved to compete a full [Junior World Rally Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_World_Rally_Championship "Junior World Rally Championship") program, driving a [Super 1600](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_1600 "Super 1600")-class [Citroën C2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn_C2 "Citroën C2") for the Equipe de France FFSA team.
Ogier debuted in the [World Rally Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Rally_Championship "World Rally Championship") at the [2008 Rally Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Rally_Mexico "2008 Rally Mexico"), winning first in the JWRC class, and becoming the first JWRC driver to take a WRC point thanks to his eighth place overall finish. He won again in [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Jordan_Rally "2008 Jordan Rally"): after a four-minute loss due to mechanical failure, he stormed back, eventually taking the victory when the leader went off the road.
After this second successive win, Ogier retired from [Rally Sardinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rally_di_Sardegna "Rally di Sardegna") with a broken steering rod. However, he restarted thanks to the SupeRally rule and finished fifth. Ogier went on to take further junior category victory in [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Rallye_Deutschland "2008 Rallye Deutschland"). He then dominated his class at Rally Catalunya scoring most of the best times, but went off the road during the last leg.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-4)
After a cautious start at his home event, the [Tour de Corse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Tour_de_Corse "2008 Tour de Corse"), Ogier clinched the Junior world champion title by placing second.
#### First WRC rally and first stage win
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: First WRC rally and first stage win")]
After winning the JWRC title, Ogier was rewarded with his first [World Rally Car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Rally_Car "World Rally Car") drive in a [Citroën C4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn_C4_WRC "Citroën C4 WRC") for [Rally GB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Rally_GB "2008 Rally GB"). He surprised the more experienced drivers by winning the first stage on the ice and taking a shock lead[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-5) for his first WRC rally. With the advantage of his road position, he kept the lead until the fifth stage, before losing time with a mechanical trouble. He eventually crashed out from eighth place on day two.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-6)

#### 2009: 1st full WRC season (1st podium) and win in Monte-Carlo (IRC)
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2009: 1st full WRC season \(1st podium\) and win in Monte-Carlo \(IRC\)")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Ogier_Ingrassia_2009.jpg/250px-Ogier_Ingrassia_2009.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ogier_Ingrassia_2009.jpg)Ogier at the [2009 Monte Carlo Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Monte_Carlo_Rally "2009 Monte Carlo Rally")
In January 2009, Ogier made a one-off appearance in the [Intercontinental Rally Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_Rally_Challenge "Intercontinental Rally Challenge"), contesting the [Monte Carlo Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_Carlo_Rally "Monte Carlo Rally"). He won the prestigious event for his first rally in a Kronos [Peugeot 207 S2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peugeot_207_S2000 "Peugeot 207 S2000").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-7)
It was only a one-off participation in IRC: for the 2009 season, Ogier was signed in WRC to capitalize on his Junior title. At the start of the season, he was supposed to take part in the first six rounds of the world championship with a C4 WRC of Citroën's satellite team, and that the remaining rallies of the season would depend on his results. Despite a few mistakes, his performances pushed the squad to confirm him for the rest of the season.
At the [Acropolis Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Acropolis_Rally "2009 Acropolis Rally"), Ogier drove to his first podium place, finishing second to [Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BP_Ford_World_Rally_Team "BP Ford World Rally Team")'s [Mikko Hirvonen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikko_Hirvonen "Mikko Hirvonen").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-8)
#### 2010: 2nd full WRC season (1st win)
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2010: 2nd full WRC season \(1st win\)")]
In January 2010, Ogier took part again in the Rallye Monte-Carlo with a Peugeot 207 S2000. After losing two minutes going off-road at the start of the race (on snow put by some spectators), he then scored a lot of stage wins and came back 45 seconds off the leader [Mikko Hirvonen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikko_Hirvonen "Mikko Hirvonen"), but eventually retired on the last day with an alternator problem.
As Monte-Carlo was still part of the IRC calendar, Ogier's [2010 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_World_Rally_Championship_season "2010 World Rally Championship season") really started in Sweden with the first round of the WRC year. The Frenchman continued in the Citroën Junior Team with the 2007 Formula One world champion [Kimi Räikkönen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimi_R%C3%A4ikk%C3%B6nen "Kimi Räikkönen") as his new teammate. He took fifth place in [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Rally_Sweden "2010 Rally Sweden") after a solid performance and clinched his second podium in [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Rally_Mexico "2010 Rally Mexico") after duelling against [Petter Solberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petter_Solberg "Petter Solberg") until the last minute. In Jordan, he took an excellent start and was lying second in the standings after the first two legs, however team orders forced him to take several minutes of penalty at a time control. He still ended in sixth position. In Turkey, Sébastien led during eleven stages, before losing three minutes with a puncture in SS15, eventually finishing fourth. At the [Rally New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Rally_New_Zealand "2010 Rally New Zealand"), he came even closer to his maiden win as he was leading before the final stage, but spun three corners before the finish and lost the win to Latvala by 2.4 seconds (third smallest gap in the history).
Ogier went on to take his debut WRC victory in the next event, the [Rally de Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Rally_de_Portugal "2010 Rally de Portugal"). Keeping the momentum from his performances in Turkey and New Zealand, he took 45 seconds from road-sweeper Sébastien Loeb on day one. Although Loeb came back, Ogier made no mistake and eventually beat him by eight seconds. He went on to win Rally della Lanterna in Italy, a guest appearance he made to gain experience on asphalt as he had always been more confident on gravel.
Given Ogier's solid results, his team spirit and [Dani Sordo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Sordo "Dani Sordo")'s disappointing performances, Citroën promoted Ogier to the factory team for the remaining three gravel rounds of the season. Subsequently, Sordo replaced Ogier in the manufacturer's junior team.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-9) It proved to be a judicious decision as Ogier took a solid second place in Finland, in front of Loeb, whereas he was fourth and third behind Sordo and Loeb on asphalt (in Bulgaria and Germany). He took his second WRC win in [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Rally_Japan "2010 Rally Japan") after a thrilling duel against Petter Solberg and impressed by his capacity to quickly adapt himself to a rally he had never raced before.
Ogier was just 43 points behind teammate [Sébastien Loeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Loeb "Sébastien Loeb") with three events to go, therefore still having a chance for the title. However, in the last three rallies he would only score nine points, making him lose two positions to Jari Matti Latvala and Petter Solberg and finishing the season in fourth place.

#### 2011: Citroën official driver
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2011: Citroën official driver")]
Ogier continued his progression in 2011. Given his performances in 2010, he was given a drive with Citroën's factory team for the full [2011 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_World_Rally_Championship_season "2011 World Rally Championship season"), replacing Dani Sordo. As he was promised to be treated equally with Loeb, the fans awaited a great battle for the title.
The DS3 WRC did not make the expected debut in [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Rally_Sweden "2011 Rally Sweden"); however, Ogier (fourth) beat Loeb (sixth), and also became the first driver to win a Power Stage. Their battle turned out to a duel in [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Rally_M%C3%A9xico "2011 Rally México") where Ogier started the last day as leader before going off the road. He went on to win the next two rallies in [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Rally_de_Portugal "2011 Rally de Portugal") and [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Jordan_Rally "2011 Jordan Rally"): with two-tenth on [Jari-Matti Latvala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jari-Matti_Latvala "Jari-Matti Latvala"), he beat the record of the smallest winning gap. fourth in Sardinia, Ogier came close to another victory in [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Rally_Argentina "2011 Rally Argentina"): while he started the last leg with a 43.7s advantage on Hirvonen, he rolled; this led him to finish with no steering wheel and cost him the win in the last stage. He ended in third position behind [Sébastien Loeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Loeb "Sébastien Loeb") and [Mikko Hirvonen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikko_Hirvonen "Mikko Hirvonen").
Ogier went on to claim victory on the [Acropolis Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Acropolis_Rally "2011 Acropolis Rally"), but his relationship with Loeb deteriorated. Following a classic WRC strategy, the Frenchman slowed down on the Saturday evening to force his teammate to open the road the day after. To do so, he based himself on Loeb's times sent by his team, while a technical problem prevented Loeb from receiving the same information. The rally ended in a controversial atmosphere as Loeb had difficulty accepting to sweep the road on these gravel stages. Loeb bounced back in [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Rally_Finland "2011 Rally Finland"), while Ogier ended in third position after a puncture during the last day. The tension between the two Citroën drivers knew their peak in [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Rallye_Deutschland "2011 Rallye Deutschland"), where Sébastien Loeb had never been beaten. Before the start of the race, the reigning World Champion announced the extension of his contract with Citroën until the end of 2013. In that media context, the brand imposed team orders at the end of the first leg, while Loeb and Ogier were separated by only seven seconds, with a big margin over their rivals. It was a beautiful battle and Sébastien Ogier did not accept being sacrificed so early and in such a disrespectful way. This is what he publicly said, giving rise to a huge controversy.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-10) The win eventually went to him, as Loeb punctured a tyre.
In [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Rally_Australia "2011 Rally Australia"), Ogier did not make the most of Sébastien Loeb going off the road as he made a mistake as well during the first day. After a thrilling climb in the standings that brought him up to ninth place and close to eighth, the team asked him to slow down at the end of the rally to let his teammate pass and score one point for the championship: he took a voluntary penalty and stopped on the side of the road for around ten minutes. Also helped by team orders, Mikko Hirvonen won the rally and therefore became a serious title contender, eight points off Loeb. Ogier took a convincing win at the [Rallye de France Alsace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Rallye_de_France "2011 Rallye de France"): after Loeb retired because of a technical problem, he resisted [Dani Sordo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Sordo "Dani Sordo")'s and [Petter Solberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petter_Solberg "Petter Solberg")'s pressure and went on to take the maximum points for the team. He also made a good operation for the Drivers' championship and left Alsace three points off the co-leaders Sébastien Loeb and Mikko Hirvonen. Two rounds before the end of the season, the championship seemed to be wide open, but Loeb did eventually clinch the title. After an engine problem in Spain and an accident in Great-Britain, Ogier ended the championship in third position with five wins (as many as Loeb) and four Power Stages' best times (the best rate of the season). His tense relationship with Citroën management led to his discharge, which was officially announced on 16 November. He was then replaced by [Mikko Hirvonen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikko_Hirvonen "Mikko Hirvonen").

### Volkswagen (2012–2016)

#### 2012
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2012")]
On 23 November 2011, [Volkswagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen "Volkswagen") subsequently announced a three-year contract with Ogier and his codriver [Julien Ingrassia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Ingrassia "Julien Ingrassia"). They became the official crew of the team to spearhead Volkswagen's WRC assault, planned for 2013. In 2012, they contested the championship in a [Škoda Fabia S2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%A0koda_Fabia_S2000 "Škoda Fabia S2000") whilst developing the new [Polo R WRC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen_Polo_R_WRC "Volkswagen Polo R WRC") for a full-time WRC season in 2013.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-11)
Ogier's 2012 season started with [Rallye Monte-Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Rallye_Monte_Carlo "2012 Rallye Monte Carlo"), where he set some good times although his Škoda Fabia S2000 was less competitive than the WRC that were battling for the win. But in the tenth stage, he went off the road in a sixth-gear sector. Ogier was unhurt; his codriver was slightly injured. Before the crash, Ogier was sixth in the overall rally standings.
In the [Rally Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Rally_Sweden "2012 Rally Sweden"), Ogier took 11th place with four minutes of margin on [Per-Gunnar Andersson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per-Gunnar_Andersson_\(rally_driver\) "Per-Gunnar Andersson \(rally driver\)"), the official winner in S2000. Sébastien Ogier took his first points of the season and the very first ones for Volkswagen Motorsport with an eighth place at the [Rally Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Rally_Mexico "2012 Rally Mexico").
In Sweden and in Mexico, Ogier had to compose with a superior status compared to the other S2000 drivers and therefore had to sweep the roads for them. This changed at the [Rally Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Rally_de_Portugal "2012 Rally de Portugal") and the situation became more equitable. He then scored a series of points scorings and regularly battled against WRC drivers. His best result came in Sardinia, where he took the fifth place – the best result of a S2000 car.
#### 2013
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2013")]
In parallel to his 2012 season with the Škoda Fabia S2000, Ogier followed an intense testing programme developing the Volkswagen Polo R WRC and preparing its debut in the championship.
Launched at Monaco at the end of 2012, the car was ready for the first round of the season, the 2013 [Rallye Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rallye_Monte_Carlo "Rallye Monte Carlo"). Despite the youth of the car and some treacherous weather conditions, Ogier finished in second position. It sounded like an ideal start, a proper relief that confirmed the promising level of the Polo.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-12)
The [2013 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Rally_Championship_season "2013 World Rally Championship season") went ahead with [Rally Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Rally_Sweden "2013 Rally Sweden"), where Ogier became the second non-Nordic winner since its creation in 1950, after Loeb's victory in 2004. His win in Sweden was also the maiden one for the Polo R WRC. He added the three bonus points of a Power Stage win and took the lead of the championship. And this was only the beginning. Ogier then took the victory in Mexico, winning 16 stages out of 23 and another double rally – Power Stage success. Same again in Portugal where he finished with more than three minutes of margin over [Mikko Hirvonen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikko_Hirvonen "Mikko Hirvonen"), second.
In Argentina, the handbrake gave problems and Ogier lost time with a straight on the mud, which cost him the lead of the rally. As Loeb won, Ogier secured some valuable points with second place. Bad luck struck again in Greece, where he lost his chances of winning as soon as in the SS1, with a puncture and a fuel alimentation problem. Thanks to the Rally 2 rule, he managed to save the tenth position and took the three bonus points of the Power Stage.
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/2013_10_05_13-24Rallye_France%2C_Parc_assistance_Colmar%2C_S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier.jpg/250px-2013_10_05_13-24Rallye_France%2C_Parc_assistance_Colmar%2C_S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2013_10_05_13-24Rallye_France,_Parc_assistance_Colmar,_S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier.jpg)Ogier, newly WRC champion at the 2013 [Rally France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rally_France "Rally France")
Ogier made his comeback on the top spot of the podium in Italy, beating [Thierry Neuville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Neuville "Thierry Neuville") and [Jari-Matti Latvala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jari-Matti_Latvala "Jari-Matti Latvala"). For the first time in his career, he dominated a rally from the first stage to the last one. He also took another win in the Power Stage.
Ogier's winning series went on in Finland, despite his co-driver's shoulder injury. He took the first victory of his career in this rally by winning more than half of the stages – and in particular the legendary Ouninpohja of which he beat the record. With two more points in the Power Stage, he extended his lead at the top of the world championship standings.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-13)
In Germany, Ogier already had an opportunity to secure the title. However he broke his front-left suspension missing a braking point during the first leg. Back on the road the following day, he climbed from 47th to 17th in the overall standings and took another Power Stage win. With Thierry Neuville second and Jari-Matti Latvala seventh, Ogier came closer to the title. In Australia, he had real chances to become champion. However, despite a thrilling race, 19 stage wins out of 22, he lost the title in the last stage: as Hirvonen punctured a tyre, Neuville took second place and Ogier therefore missed the title for one point.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-14)
Ogier eventually won the 2013 championship in the first stage of Rally France (which happened to be the bonus-points-rewarding Power Stage) because second-placed Thierry Neuville could not catch Ogier anymore even with rally wins.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-15) The Frenchman ended the season with some more victories in France, Spain and, for the first time in his career, Wales.
Ogier ended the season with nine wins, 11 podiums, 111 special stages wins (46,83% of the season), seven Power Stages wins and a total number of 28 points grabbed in these particular stages, and a total of 290 points in the championship, a record for WRC.
#### 2014
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2014")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/22/2014_rally_sweden_by_2eight_dsc9422.jpg/250px-2014_rally_sweden_by_2eight_dsc9422.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2014_rally_sweden_by_2eight_dsc9422.jpg)Ogier at the 2014 Rally Sweden
Ogier cautiously considers that a title is harder to defend than to win. However, his victory in the Rallye Monte-Carlo confirmed his leading position in WRC at the start of the 2014 season.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-16) Unlike in 2009 this legendary rally was part of the WRC, which made it a very special moment for the reigning World Champion. Despite a wrong tyre choice on day one, he impressed with his climb in the standings and entered Monaco as a winner. Icing on the cake, the start was given in his native town of Gap and the first part of the race was back in the Hautes-Alpes.
Ogier made a mistake during Rally Sweden hitting a snowbank while leading and retrograded to the 20th position. His determination eventually led him to the sixth final place. His revenge came as soon as Rally Mexico: he took the lead in the first leg and increased his margin until finishing with a big margin on his opponents. He also won the Power Stage and was back at the lead of the championship in front of Latvala.
Ogier managed to increase his overall lead on his teammate on the next round, Rally Portugal. He took the overall victory and won the Power Stage again, while Latvala went off the road. Rally Portugal was again synonymous of a win for the Frenchman – the fourth one for him on this round, which brought him closer to [Markku Alen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markku_Alen "Markku Alen")'s record of five successes. Conversely Rally Argentina is one of the rare rallies of the season (with Rally Poland) where Ogier never won. In very hard conditions, he took second place and the Power Stage win. He was back on the top step of the podium in Italy,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-17) despite a tough first leg in which he had to open the road and sweep a slippery sandy surface. In Poland, he won both the rally and the Power Stage, to get a 50-point lead in the championship.
In Finland, Ogier scored the points of the second place and took another Power Stage win. His lead in the championship was unchanged after the next round, Rally Germany, where Ogier and Latvala both retired going off the road. However Volkswagen was assured that the Drivers' title would go to one of the team's drivers (Ogier, Latvala or Mikkelsen). The German squad secured the Manufacturers' title on the following round, in Australia, as Ogier was back on the top step of the podium. His first attempt in securing the championship failed though, as he was hit by a gearbox sensor failure at the start of Rally France. Despite the time lost, he managed to secure the Power Stage points. The relief came on his second try, in Catalonia. As they won the penultimate round of the season, Ogier and [Julien Ingrassia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Ingrassia "Julien Ingrassia") secured their second title.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-18) Ogier became the eighth driver to take a second crown, the fourth to do so two years in a row. Ingrassia is the sole French codriver crowned twice. The Frenchman ended the season in style with a win in Wales. With eight wins, ten podiums and 94 stage wins, Ogier had a 49-point margin in the final standings.
Volkswagen renewed the contract of Ogier and their other crews.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-19)
#### 2015
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: 2015")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier_Rally_Italy_2015_002.jpg/250px-S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier_Rally_Italy_2015_002.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier_Rally_Italy_2015_002.jpg)Sébastien Ogier at the 2015 Rally Italy
In 2015, Ogier stayed involved in WRC with the Volkswagen Motorsport team, codriven by Ingrassia. Together, they won the first round of the season, the [Rallye Monte-Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rallye_Monte-Carlo "Rallye Monte-Carlo"). The new Polo R WRC was immediately successful and so was the world champion crew despite the rivalry of [Sébastien Loeb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Loeb "Sébastien Loeb"), who made a punctual comeback to rallying.
Ogier went ahead with another win in Sweden, where he came out as the winner in the very last stage, when Andreas Mikkelsen made a late mistake.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-20) Three out of three: it was a hat-trick for the Frenchman who also won Rally Mexico.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-21) This was his fifth consecutive win since 2014 Rally Catalunya and the third in a row in Mexico.
Rally Argentina marked the end of the series, as mechanical problems pushed Ogier to retirement. He ended in 17th position and added the three bonus points of a Power Stage win. He won the Power Stage again on the following rally, in Portugal, while climbing the second final place. In addition to the disadvantage of sweeping a very sandy surface, the Frenchman lost time with a puncture before producing an impressive comeback to end 8.2s off the winner. This enabled him to confirm his leading position in the championship.
Ogier managed to come back to victory in Italy. [Hayden Paddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayden_Paddon "Hayden Paddon") produced his best performance to date and led the rally for a long time, but Ogier eventually took the win in the last leg and added again the Power Stage victory to his tally. Another rally and Power Stage double win came in Poland, while in Finland he had to settle for the second place overall. He took another Power Stage success though (the seventh successive) to leave Finland with an 89-point lead in the championship. He led VW to a 1–2–3 finish on Rally Germany, and went on to take the title on the next round with a win in Rally Australia. After taking the lead, Ogier and Ingrassia won all the remaining stages to take their 31st WRC win and their 3rd title. At the same moment, Volkswagen secured the Manufacturer title.
Rally France was not so lucky as Ogier suffered a gearbox failure at the end of day one. Despite a ten-minute penalty which relegated him to 55th position, he managed to end in 12th and won three more stages including the Power Stage. Sébastien Ogier then led Rally Spain for the last two legs but made a mistake in the very last stage. He was forced to retire after hitting a guardrail, a crash in which he and his codriver were unhurt. The season ended with a soaked Wales Rally GB where the Frenchmen won again. They dedicated their victory to the victims of Paris's attacks occurred on 13 November, during the rally weekend.
#### 2016
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 2016")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier_2016-07-30_001.jpg/250px-S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier_2016-07-30_001.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier_2016-07-30_001.jpg)Sébastien Ogier at the 2016 Rally Finland
Still teamed up with Ingrassia in the Volkswagen Motorsport squad for the fourth successive year, Ogier started the season with his third successive win on Rally Monte-Carlo. He then took another success on Rally Sweden, which had been shortened due to a lack of snow. In Mexico, Ogier had to sweep very dusty roads again but still took second place behind Latvala, also winning his third Power Stage out of three rallies. His first place in the championship penalized him again in Argentina, where he took second place, and then again in Portugal and Italy where he finished third. Rally Poland was even more difficult and ended up with a sixth place, before a small mistake cost him a lot in Finland, with no points scored.
Ogier was back to the win in Germany, on Volkswagen's home soil. First full-tarmac rally of the season, it was won by the French pair for the second year in a row as they managed in the best way some very changeable road conditions. Ogier went on to win in Corsica after dominating the rally from start to finish. He was again on the top step of the podium in Spain and clinched the world champion title for the fourth time. His victory at Wales Rally GB brought the Manufacturers' title to Volkswagen, this also for the fourth successive year.
In the days following this success, Volkswagen announced its withdrawal from WRC.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-22)
### M-Sport Ford (2017–2018)
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: M-Sport Ford \(2017–2018\)")]
#### 2017
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: 2017")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/2017_Rally_Australia_%2819%29.jpg/250px-2017_Rally_Australia_%2819%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2017_Rally_Australia_\(19\).jpg)Ogier at the [2017 Rally Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Rally_Australia "2017 Rally Australia")
On 12 December 2016, Ogier announced he would be driving the new Ford Fiesta WRC for M-Sport Ford during the 2017 season.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-23)
On the first rally of the championship, Monte-Carlo, Ogier brought M-Sport Ford back to victory for the first time since the 2012 Wales Rally GB, taking the 39th victory of his personal career and the fifth one on this rally (including one not counting for WRC) with three different manufacturers.
The following months were made of highs and lows, with two wins and less special stage victories than in the past but nine podiums (after Wales Rally GB) that enabled him to score regular points. The second win came in Rally Portugal, where he equaled [Markku Alén](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markku_Al%C3%A9n "Markku Alén") five victories and reached win number 40 in his career. Thanks to his consistency, he managed to clinch his fifth successive title, celebrating the success at Wales Rally GB,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-24) while M-Sport Ford also secured the manufacturers title.
#### 2018
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: 2018")]
> It’s been an incredible [2018] season, so close. Not so long ago we were thinking it was going to be tough to grab this title but we never gave up. We gave everything, with a fantastic team behind us who kept fighting and in the end we grabbed it in the last rally. It’s so emotional.
— FIA WRC NEWS – 18 November 2018[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-25)
2018 started very well, but turned out to be a gruelling year for Ogier. He won Monte Carlo to take the lead of the WRC drivers championship, but a lowly tenth position in Sweden opened the door for rival [Thierry Neuville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Neuville "Thierry Neuville"); who lead the championship for most of the year. Two more wins followed for Ogier, but a retirement in Portugal meant Neuville took the advantage.
The second half of the season saw mixed conditions, leaving the championship contenders struggling for points, particularly in Turkey.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-26) A commanding win for Ogier in Wales finally broke the deadlock, and he began to win back points towards Neuville. Three successive wins for [Ott Tänak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ott_T%C3%A4nak "Ott Tänak"), and a continued resolve by the Estonian, meant the drivers championship depended on the final result of the season finale in Australia. Ogier remained in good humour, and gained the advantage as rivals went off in muddy conditions, ultimately winning the 2018 WRC Drivers Championship.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-27) Ogier and co-driver Ingrassia had successfully defended their championship titles for the sixth consecutive year.
### 2019
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: 2019")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/54._RallyRACC_Catalunya_-_Ogier_S%C3%A9bastien.jpg/250px-54._RallyRACC_Catalunya_-_Ogier_S%C3%A9bastien.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:54._RallyRACC_Catalunya_-_Ogier_S%C3%A9bastien.jpg)Ogier at the [2019 Rally Catalunya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Rally_Catalunya "2019 Rally Catalunya")
On 28 September 2018, it was announced that Ogier and Ingrassia will rejoin the Citroën World Rally Team for the 2019 season. This will mark the return of the six-time world champions to the French manufacturer after seven years.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-28) Ogier claimed his sixth consecutive win at Monte Carlo, which also marked the 100th world rally success for Citroën. After an early retirement in Sweden, he won at Mexico and climbed to the podium at the next three rounds.
But despite claiming another victory at Turkey, Ogier had been unhappy with his car during the season. At Spain, he failed to defend his title. After leading on the opening stage, his C3 WRC crawled throughout the morning loop after losing hydraulics. Ogier finished eighth in the rally, and with Ott Tänak securing his maiden WRC title by finishing second with a power stage victory, the Frenchman's title chances were effectively over.
On 30 November 2019, Ogier told _[Autosport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autosport "Autosport")_ he planned to leave Citroën for Toyota with a year left on his contract.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-29) He blamed mixed results in the latter half of the season on slow development, a lack of performance, and a lack of communication in the team. Citroën responded by immediately withdrawing from the WRC from the date of Ogier's departure.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-30)
### Toyota Gazoo Racing (2020–)
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Toyota Gazoo Racing \(2020–\)")]
#### 2020
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: 2020")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/SebOgierRallySweden2020%281%29.jpg/250px-SebOgierRallySweden2020%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SebOgierRallySweden2020\(1\).jpg)Ogier driving at the [2020 Rally Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Rally_Sweden "2020 Rally Sweden")
Amid speculations and statements about his retirement from the sport, Ogier signed for Toyota for the 2020 season, with an option for 2021. The six-time world champion claimed second place at his home event of Rallye Monte-Carlo, and claimed the podium four further times during a shortened seven event championship. Contender [Elfyn Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elfyn_Evans "Elfyn Evans") took the lead for most of the season, but skidded on ice at the final event at the Monza race track, with only two stages still to go. Evans waved Ogier's car to slow down at the same corner where his car had floundered off the road. Ogier later remarked that this action saved his car from a similar incident, and Ogier and co-driver Ingrassia lifted their seventh world title at this event.
#### 2021
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: 2021")]
In 2021, Ogier picked up an option on his contract but announced plans to retire at the end of the season. He began the season as the six-time defending winner in [Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_Carlo_Rally "Monte Carlo Rally")[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-32) and started off with a 50th career victory, the seventh one in this rally. Next month, however, he had a poor showing in the snowy stages of the [2021 Arctic Rally Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Arctic_Rally_Finland "2021 Arctic Rally Finland"), including a crash near the end of SS8 that cost him almost ten minutes.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-33) He claimed wins at Croatia, Italy, Kenya and Monza later on, and finished third at Portugal and Greece, earning his eighth title over teammate [Elfyn Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elfyn_Evans "Elfyn Evans").
#### 2022
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: 2022")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Oreca_07_-_Lilou_Wadoux%2C_Sebastien_Ogier_%26_Charles_Milesi_at_Ford_Chicane_at_the_2022_Le_Mans_%2854273402623%29.jpg/250px-Oreca_07_-_Lilou_Wadoux%2C_Sebastien_Ogier_%26_Charles_Milesi_at_Ford_Chicane_at_the_2022_Le_Mans_%2854273402623%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Oreca_07_-_Lilou_Wadoux,_Sebastien_Ogier_&_Charles_Milesi_at_Ford_Chicane_at_the_2022_Le_Mans_\(54273402623\).jpg)Ogier driving at the [2022 24 Hours of Le Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_24_Hours_of_Le_Mans "2022 24 Hours of Le Mans")
As he wished to spend more time with his family, Sébastien Ogier decided to commit to a partial programme in the WRC starting in the 2022 season, still with Toyota.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-34) He only competes in six rallies that year, and at the same time, turned his attention to endurance racing in order to learn a new discipline and discover the 24 Hours of Le Mans in particular.
Often battling at the front of the field, he only secured one victory in 2022. Success eluded him by a narrow margin at the Monte Carlo Rally, where he finished second after losing control following a puncture in the penultimate special stage. Nevertheless, it was his first podium finish with his new co-driver, [Benjamin Veillas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Veillas "Benjamin Veillas"), who took over from [Julien Ingrassia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Ingrassia "Julien Ingrassia"), who had co-driven Ogier since the beginning of his career in 2005, retired from competition after their 2021 title.
Punctures prevented him from winning in Portugal and then in [2022 Safari Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Safari_Rally "2022 Safari Rally"). He then returned to the [2022 Rally New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Rally_New_Zealand "2022 Rally New Zealand"), which he had not competed in since 2010, the year in which he came close to securing his first WRC victory. This time, he finished second. He finally broke his duck at the [2022 Rally Catalunya (World Rally Championship)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Rally_Catalunya_\(World_Rally_Championship\) "2022 Rally Catalunya \(World Rally Championship\)"), where he clinched his first victory alongside Benjamin Veillas, his first without Julien Ingrassia at his side. To finish the season at the [2022 Rally Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Rally_Japan "2022 Rally Japan"), however, he welcomed a new co-driver, [Vincent Landais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Landais "Vincent Landais"), previously associated with Pierre-Louis Loubet. Together, they finished fourth in the last asphalt rally of the season. Sebastien Ogier classified 6th in the 2022 championship, with 97 points.
#### 2023
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: 2023")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/WRC_Central_European_Rallye_2023_Nr._17_%283%29.jpg/250px-WRC_Central_European_Rallye_2023_Nr._17_%283%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:WRC_Central_European_Rallye_2023_Nr._17_\(3\).jpg)Ogier at the [2023 Central European Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Central_European_Rally "2023 Central European Rally")
Ogier decided to continue to contest selected events in 2023, with [Vincent Landais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Landais "Vincent Landais") remaining his co-driver. Ogier's first event was the [2023 Monte Carlo Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Monte_Carlo_Rally "2023 Monte Carlo Rally"), which he led from start to finish, despite Rovanperä's late push. He won the rally for the ninth time, becoming the most successful driver in the event's history and surpassing the previous record held by Sébastien Loeb.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-35) After Julien Ingrassia and Benjamin Veillas, this is the third co-driver to join the list of his victories.
Ogier later competed in the [2023 Rally Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Rally_Mexico "2023 Rally Mexico"), which he won for the seventh time, breaking another record of Sébastien Loeb after taking the lead from SS11 following the crash of rival [Esapekka Lappi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esapekka_Lappi "Esapekka Lappi").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-37) He would win again in [Safari Rally Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Safari_Rally "2024 Safari Rally") later in the year and finish fifth in the championship despite missing five rounds.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-38)
#### 2024
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: 2024")]
He continued this part-time programme in 2024, starting with a second place finish at [2024 Monte Carlo Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Monte_Carlo_Rally "2024 Monte Carlo Rally") after an emotional weekend following the death of his uncle, the man who had given him his first go-kart as a child.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-39) Back in [Croatia Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Croatia_Rally "2024 Croatia Rally") three months later, he won a closely fought rally, with Thierry Neuville and Elfyn Evans both crashing out on the final day.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-40) This was Ogier's 100th podium finish in the WRC and his 59th victory.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-41) He won again in [Rally de Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Rally_de_Portugal "2024 Rally de Portugal") for the sixth time, breaking the previous record held by Markku Alén,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-42) and [Rally Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Rally_Finland "2024 Rally Finland") during the season,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-43) and was even in contention for the title for a while before suffering several setbacks at the end of the season and finishing 4th overall.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-44)
#### 2025
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: 2025")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/2025_Toyota_GR_Yaris_Rally_1_Ogier.jpg/250px-2025_Toyota_GR_Yaris_Rally_1_Ogier.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2025_Toyota_GR_Yaris_Rally_1_Ogier.jpg)Ogier at the [2025 Rally Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Rally_Japan "2025 Rally Japan")
In 2025, Ogier and his co-driver Vincent Landais once again embarked on a partial season, missing three rallies in the first part of the championship. Nevertheless, they racked up numerous podium finishes and victories, to the point where they officially decided to do all the remaining rallies and try to chase the title.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-45)
Ogier and Landais were finally crowned WRC world champions at the end of the [Rally Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Rally_Saudi_Arabia "2025 Rally Saudi Arabia"), where they were battling it out with two other Toyota drivers, [Elfyn Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elfyn_Evans "Elfyn Evans") and [Kalle Rovanperä](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalle_Rovanper%C3%A4 "Kalle Rovanperä"). The Frenchman ultimately won by four points in the championship, equalling his compatriot Sébastien Loeb with nine WRC world titles.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-46)

  * **29–30 October 2011:** He took part in the last round of the French GT Championship at the [Paul Ricard circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_Paul_Ricard "Circuit Paul Ricard"). In these 2 GT Tour races he drove a [Ferrari F430 Scuderia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_F430 "Ferrari F430") of the team _Sport Garage_ , as the teammate of Lionel Comole, President of the _Fondation Arthritis_ and amatorial driver. Ogier also contested the finale round of the F4 French Championship with a single-seater of the _Auto Sport Academy_ (i.e. the car that helped him to improve his late braking in corner entering on asphalt during his summer tests).
  * **16 July 2011:** He took part in the Moscow City Racing with Citroën. The _Race of Stars_ (as it was called) was held close to the [Kremlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kremlin "Kremlin").
  * **11 December 2011:** He took the 9th place of the ERDF Master-Kart of [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris")-[Bercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palais_omnisports_de_Paris-Bercy "Palais omnisports de Paris-Bercy"), against drivers coming from all kind of motorsport series.
  * **24–26 May 2013:** He contested the Monaco round of the Porsche Supercup, the series that is traditionally held before the [Formula 1 Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco_Grand_Prix "Monaco Grand Prix"). After a 14th place in qualifying, he ended 13th out of 26 drivers in the race.
  * **23–25 May 2014:** He took part in a round of the ADAC GT Masters, on the [Lausitzring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lausitzring "Lausitzring") circuit. He drove an Audi R8 LMS Ultra of the Prosperia C. Abt Racing team, together with [Markus Winkelhock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markus_Winkelhock "Markus Winkelhock"). Together, they took the 13th place in Race 1 and the 8th in Race 2.
  * **20–22 June 2014:** Ogier took part in a second Porsche Supercup race, this time at the Red Bull Ring. Just like in 2013 at Monaco, he joins the Deutsche Post Project 1 team to drive a Porsche 911 GT3.
  * **21–23 September 2018:** After a test in August, he competed in a [DTM round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Deutsche_Tourenwagen_Masters "2018 Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters") at the Red Bull Ring in a Mercedes-AMG C63, finishing 12th in Race 1 and 17th in Race 2.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-53)


## Personal life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier&action=edit&section=49 "Edit section: Personal life")]
Ogier is married to German television presenter [Andrea Kaiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Kaiser "Andrea Kaiser"). Their son Tim was born on 13 June 2016.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-54)
Since 2014, Sébastien Ogier has been a patron for [Make-A-Wish Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Make-A-Wish_Foundation "Make-A-Wish Foundation") in France, a charity granting wishes for children with critical illnesses. In 2021 he also donated €10,000 of his winnings from the [2021 Safari Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Safari_Rally "2021 Safari Rally") to each of two charities, the Nakuru Children's Project which focuses on children's education in Kenya and the [Ol Pejeta Conservancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ol_Pejeta_Conservancy "Ol Pejeta Conservancy") which protects Kenyan wildlife.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9bastien_Ogier#cite_note-55)
